source.title: Rethinking the Role of Scale for In-Context Learning: An Interpretability-based Case Study at 66 Billion Scale
source.authors: Hritik Bansal; Karthik Gopalakrishnan; Saket Dingliwal; S. Bodapati; K. Kirchhoff; Dan Roth

record.tranche_reason: The study applies Olsson et al.'s prefix-matching and copying score framework to OPT-66B, a new model and scale. It adapts the sequence sampling setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports task-accuracy effects from pruning attention heads and FFNs, but those pruning results do not isolate induction heads, so they are not rows for these claim versions. The induction-related results are the prefix-matching and copying measurements, their retention under task-importance-ranked pruning, and the reported differences across tasks.
record.test_reason: The study applies Olsson et al.'s prefix-matching and copying scores to OPT-66B, a new family and scale. It finds a sparse set of heads scoring high on both, which bears on V4 (induction heads appear in other model families and sizes). It does not study small attention-only models, head composition, training dynamics, or induction-head ablation effects on ICL.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find a sparse set of OPT-66B heads that score high on both prefix matching and copying. These heads overlap, to varying degrees, with heads ranked important (by gradient sensitivity) for 14 tasks, which the authors read as support for induction heads' generality and as showing they are not the only heads with such capabilities. They also conclude that about 70% of heads and 20% of FFNs can be pruned with little loss, and that LLMs may be under-trained for ICL.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Olsson et al. prefix-matching and copying scoring approach, but evaluates 100 random sequences of varying lengths rather than 10 fixed-length sequences of length 25; the raw scores are not scaled to the range -1 to 1.
record.method_sensitivity: Task-specific pruning rankings produce different induction-capacity retention slopes across tasks; the authors report greater task reliance for HellaSwag and ReCoRD than for OpenBookQA.

fits_no_version.finding: Heads ranked unimportant for 14 few-shot tasks (by gradient importance) carry little prefix-matching score: most prefix-matching capacity remains after pruning the least important 20%, with a sharp decline after 40%. Copying capacity declines quickly regardless of ranking. Overlap varies by task, with HellaSwag and ReCoRD showing smaller initial slopes than OpenBookQA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In large LMs, heads with high prefix-matching scores are concentrated among heads important for few-shot downstream tasks, while copying ability is spread more widely.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Only OPT-66B is tested. Prefix matching and copying are scored separately, and the study does not causally test the complete induction circuit or remove induction-scored heads to measure their direct effect on ICL. The induction-score values are shown in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: None of the induction-related results meeting the row criteria were left out.

untested.parts: Other model families, other sizes, multiple training runs, other architectures or modalities. Only one OPT-66B checkpoint is scored.
Small attention-only models, composition with a previous-token head, and a causal test of the full [A][B]…[A]→[B] circuit.
ICL measured as loss falling with token index, and any causal test that induction heads account for most of it.
No ablation of induction-scored heads versus other heads on few-shot task accuracy.
No variation of training data or training setup.

record.verdict_notes: Overlap is correlational: task importance is gradient-based, and induction heads are never ablated directly, so V3 and V6 cannot be judged. The reader's V1 links were wrong because OPT-66B is not a small attention-only model. The scores are not rescaled to [-1, 1] as in Olsson et al., and no numeric thresholds or values are given; results appear only as heatmaps.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures prefix matching and copying separately; it does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or establish the complete [A][B] … [A] → [B] circuit causally.
Training-time formation, abruptness, in-context-learning transition timing, and the loss-curve bump.

Whether induction heads cause most in-context learning, including the loss-falling-with-token-index measure; the study reports overlap with task-important heads, not an induction-head-specific causal test of most ICL.
Universality across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities; only OPT-66B is studied.
Comparisons of training data or training setups and their effects on induction-head formation or persistence of ICL.
A causal comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms for few-shot task learning.
Whether formation consists of multiple transitions or sub-steps.

rows.subject: OPT-66B
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-head prefix-matching scores on repeated random token sequences.

conditions.value: randomly sampled from vocabulary after excluding the 4% most and least common tokens

rows.note: The text says a small subset of heads have high prefix-matching scores, located in upper layers (31+).
rows.check: Relinked from V1 to V4. OPT-66B is not a small attention-only transformer, and no previous-token composition is tested. The row shows a small subset of heads in layers 31+ with high prefix-matching scores. Figure only; no baseline.

rows.subject: OPT-66B
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention-head copying scores on random token sequences.

conditions.value: randomly sampled from vocabulary after excluding the 4% most and least common tokens

rows.note: The text reports relatively more heads with high copying scores than with high prefix-matching scores; most high-copying heads are in upper layers (41+).
rows.check: Relinked from V1 to V4. Copying alone is not induction, but read together with R1 the authors identify a sparse set of plausible induction heads. Many heads copy, mostly in layers 41+. Figure only.

rows.subject: OPT-66B
rows.operation_detail: Pruned heads from least to most important using aggregate task-specific importance rankings and tracked retained prefix-matching capacity.
rows.measure: Percentage of total prefix-matching score retained
rows.note: The authors report that much of the total prefix-matching score remains after 20% of the least important heads are removed, with decline becoming sharp after the 40% pruning mark.
rows.check: Measures overlap between prefix-matching capacity and gradient-based task-importance rankings, not induction behaviour or its causal role in ICL. Heads are not ablated by induction score. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.value: The authors report smaller initial slopes for HellaSwag and ReCoRD than for OpenBookQA.

tranche.reason: Tests induction behaviour in pretrained OPT-66B, extending the model family and scale with adapted sequence sampling and copying-score normalization.

source_check.notes: Induction-score magnitudes are figure-only; no uncertainty is reported for these scores. Copying scores are not rescaled to [-1, 1], and task-importance overlap does not establish that induction heads causally carry most in-context learning.
